title: USB host: keyboard, mouse, CDC, and flash storage

spans.text: A USB host enumerates peripherals, supplies bus power, and communicates through class drivers. ESP32-S2/S3 OTG boards can support keyboards, mice, CDC adapters, and MSC drives.

Arduino-ESP32 TinyUSB host includes `USBHostHIDKeyboard`, `USBHostHIDMouse`, `USBHostSerialClass`, and MSC support. Register HID handlers before `USBHost.begin()`, check startup, and call `USBHost.task()` repeatedly in `loop()`. Mount an MSC filesystem only after the drive is detected; close files and call `end()` before unplugging.

The host must supply 5 V VBUS and adequate current. Check the board schematic for a host power switch, protection, and OTG connector; several peripherals may need a powered hub. A classic UNO or ordinary USB-UART connector is not a USB host.

spans.title: Important safety and compatibility note
spans.text: USB host requires an OTG-capable ESP32-S2/S3/P4 board; the USB device stack cannot own the same peripheral simultaneously. Without board VBUS power, attached devices will not work. Test with peripherals you own.
